scope: Declaration inventory: all Web bundle inserted declarations, standard preset top-level plugins and nested groups, standard delegation children, Android disabled entries, and insert/override rows from base, headless, sdk-minimal, sdk-app and acp-app bundle patches. Repeated plugins are recorded once per source declaration. Web top-level override values, alternate Web preset internals, user profile overlays, CLI interaction behavior and behavior outside these declarations remain outside this ledger. Coverage does not certify Android migration or feature completion. Capability groups link declarations to user outcomes; alternative launch configurations are explicitly classified without waiving shared Android behavior. The Linux group covers delivery outside the declaration inventory.
evidencePolicy: Each evidence level is a manual, scoped claim. partial records known overlap without certifying equivalence; unverified is explicit. Portable tools, native references, recorded skill rows and workspace changes and filesystem tools cite executed host composition or behavior checks, not device acceptance for their new controls. Existing device observations remain narrowly described. File existence never upgrades evidence; inventory validation is not feature completion. Optional bundle assessments record source composition only and leave every execution evidence level unverified. not-applicable requires an explicit native-entrypoint exclusion; it is not completion and does not discharge related capabilities.

entries.note: Android ACTION_VIEW offers an external app for supported, authorized files with cancellable staging and FileProvider access. Desktop file reveal/association behavior differs, and device launch and provider handling remain unverified.

Native account reads and sign-in exist. The explicit authorization-link fallback carries the active palette and preserves Host query parameters; account balances follow original two-decimal and sub-cent display rules without changing raw values. Account and sidebar share a bounded, credential-free avatar load with failure fallback, explicit retry and stale-result rejection. A frame-wide account notice follows live ACCOUNT_QUOTA Session failures, offers the native top-up action when the account is confirmed, and keeps browser-launch failures retryable under keyless Flutter tests. Generic QUOTA shows only a short toast. Full original settings, onboarding, Custom Tab and device behavior remain unverified.
Native theme preferences and FlClash surfaces implement the requested mobile presentation; original preference equivalence remains unverified.

Native external-keyboard handling covers original new-session Mod+N and search Mod+K, plus mobile sidebar Mod+B, settings Mod+Comma, composer focus, and contextual Escape. For an existing active Session it also maps original files Mod+P, browser Mod+T, and terminal Ctrl+Backquote to their mobile resource pages; an unsaved draft cannot open Session resources. Focused Flutter tests pass. Original workspace-add, rename, fork, archive, configurable shortcut recording, modal reference, and physical-device keyboard behavior remain unverified or unmapped.
Native floating shell exists; the original complete layout/navigation surface remains to be checked.
Flutter renders mapped surfaces, but arbitrary original client-plugin slot registrations do not automatically become native UI.
Native session observations exist; full original paging and all projections require feature-level review.
Native workspace and conversation navigation exists; per-action parity and restoration remain separately verified.

A per-Session mobile tab strip lazily opens files, changes, skills, tasks, terminals and a remote browser. Mounted views survive tab switches; per-runtime tab identities restore in memory without reviving Agent or terminal work. Flutter tests cover Session isolation, re-entry, reconnect, close and state retention. Desktop split/float panes and embedded browser controls are not mapped; terminal/browser device behavior remains unverified.

Original reader bundles run in a Session-bound document-only surface with host rendering and original Gateway evidence. Same-Session links, line navigation, source-position restoration and rejected cross-Session links have host coverage. Build 32 displayed synthetic text; Build 33 displayed Markdown, followed same-Session links to text line 220 and returned at the source position. The original Office provider converted a synthetic DOCX through authorized Session reads, the Android-profile Gateway and bounded PDF byte transfer on the host; Android runs the pinned kit in a child process so its WASM heap is released on exit. This does not reduce conversion-time device memory pressure. Android WebView rendering and device memory behavior remain unverified. The accepted shared ui-settings.enabled preference now selects static or interactive HTML without remounting the reader; original bounded local JS/CSS loading runs inside an opaque sandboxed iframe with host-browser evidence. The Android document WebView still denies external HTTP(S) resources. Original DSH permits browser-loaded HTTPS HTML resources and external Markdown images; a tested URL and redirect preflight now exists, but resource-type classification, DNS-to-TLS pinning, browser origin and request semantics, network authorization, bounded transport and disposal cancellation remain before it can be wired into WebView. Interactive HTML rendering needs device acceptance.

Session resources offer remote HTTP(S) address entry and page-local launch history. AndroidX Custom Tabs owns network loading, navigation and cookies, keeping untrusted pages outside the App WebView/document bridge; direct local/private-address input is rejected. A remote redirect can still contact a local service, whose protection is server-side authentication and origin checks. The original embedded/docked browser is not migrated. Custom Tabs launch and lifecycle have host compile evidence only, no device acceptance.

The mobile Session resource page opens process-backed terminals and projects bounded xterm cells with ANSI/RGB colors, emphasis, inverse video and cursor position. Host runtime and Flutter tests cover projection, alternate buffers, text copy, reconnect ownership, acknowledged live IME text, application-cursor keys and supported xterm/OSC color query replies. OSC hexadecimal colors scale each channel correctly, and creating a selected system Shell no longer depends on unrelated candidate probes. Program palette, cursor and DECSET mouse settings persist with the PTY across page re-entry. Hardware mouse and stylus button, drag, motion and wheel events use SGR reports when the program enables 1006 and a tracking mode; touch keeps scrolling. Full VT/OSC semantics, legacy mouse encodings and desktop dock behavior remain absent; device IME/PTY/pointer execution and process-tree cleanup remain unverified.

Current Session files use the original cold Session cwd and workspaceFiles list/change feed. Native same-page navigation restores each directory's last read-only listing while it revalidates through the original service; restored rows cannot be opened until relisted, and a changed Session cwd clears those snapshots. Original-service host smoke passes. Build 32 listed the test Session cwd and opened its existing text file on the phone; nested device navigation and remaining file interactions are unverified.

Native structured configuration pages exist. Restoring a user override previews the descriptor's inherited value without writing it; focused form tests cover switches and finite choices. Workspace-change visibility and reads use the original ui-settings/enabled value with no App-only default. Schema accessibility does not establish complete settings workflow parity.

General Settings reads and writes the original revisioned ui-settings.enabled preference through a native switch. The shared value gates Session trajectory visibility and built-in uncustomized PTC/Minimal preset choices as well as workspace-change presentation; it is not a tool permission. Disabling conditionally changes an uncustomized built-in PTC/Minimal default to a healthy Standard preset through the original revisioned settings service; customized, unknown or changed defaults require manual review. Contributed General rows, onboarding and device acceptance remain incomplete.

Native provider/model/credential forms call shared services. A catalog outage retains provider settings and the saved default but blocks model changes until a bounded or manual retry succeeds; widget tests cover this separation. Full original action and device recovery coverage is not certified here.
Native shared package operations exist; device install, lifecycle scripts, and third-party compatibility remain unverified.

Native Host snapshot inventory shows preset-first entries, optional global entries, full entry and module identities, conditional disablement, runtime phase, discovery failures and preset-provider relationships in read-only detail. Focused widget tests cover these projections; device behavior and remaining original presentation interactions are unverified.
Native composer and transcript exist; resource actions, all context projections and view switching remain incomplete.

Native decisions, plan-review actions, recommended question options and original answer labels have focused tests. A private write-ahead marker persists possible reply submission across Host restarts and blocks duplicate delivery for identified requests; a started marker does not prove delivery and may leave an unanswered request blocked until authoritative reconciliation exists. Full request-variant comparison and device behavior remain incomplete.

Native transcript renders authored text, Markdown, tool rows, recorded skill and Session reference chips, delivered files and original workspace-change summaries. Settled local Markdown images load through the original Session-scoped workspaceFiles stat/readBytes service with bounded bytes and version checks, then open the native zoom viewer; failures can retry or open the original file. Model retry rows now count down only for an active attempt in the current running turn, expand to a credential-safe failure and delay, and remain static on historical replay. Confirmed skill names and Session labels come from the original log, not the current catalog. Remote Markdown images remain explicit external links rather than inline fetches; file-image hover cards, remaining original actions and phone acceptance are incomplete.
The user-requested Pocket Harness branding replaces the original visible brand in native UI.
Original attachment receipts are used with Android picking and historical reads; all media/limit/recovery device paths remain open.
Native paired tool records and details exist; generic fallback does not implement every original keyed tool presentation.
Only generic tool details are available; original Cordis-specific editing and workflow presentation are not fully migrated.

Native present cards fold original persisted events by completed turn, preserve exact file paths and open the Session reader. Changed-file cards and native diffs use the original announcement coordinates and summary/diff service, gated by shared ui-settings/enabled. Captured bytes do not survive a service restart; outside Git, file-operation capture excludes arbitrary Shell changes. Original-profile host smoke and widget tests cover read-only behavior, cancellation, cold unavailable results and shared preference changes; device acceptance remains unverified.
Shared workspace/session registry operations exist; all original lifecycle actions remain subject to individual acceptance.

Existing Session workflow run/start/end and member events replay into a read-only run/stage/member view, including pagination and interruption semantics. Host-tested navigation from a historical run to a still-running child Session revalidates parent ownership and connection generation. Android still cannot create runs because PTC/workflow execution is disabled; device behavior remains unverified.

Inline slash command candidates and file/Session at-reference selection now use the original catalog with cancellation, drill-down and same-token dismissal behavior under host tests. Full keyboard candidate navigation, all original source arbitration and device behavior remain unverified.

Runtime command catalog and dispatch are reused. Manual /compact now folds its correlated checkpoint and summary into one compact, expandable result row; partial-history recovery, mismatched summaries and error outcomes have focused host tests. Other command-specific surfaces and device behavior remain unverified.

Native slash suggestions and a searchable picker use original skills/list, preserve user-only skills, insert literal /name text and keep command precedence. Recorded injection batches confirm sent skill chips; dedicated skill rows use original call/result data and open recorded instructions, while reference previews open the current provider file. Host replay and widget checks cover these distinctions. Build 33 displayed a synthetic user-only skill and opened its provider file on the phone; composer invocation and the new historical chips/rows still need device acceptance.

Native sidebar exposes the active parent's child catalog. A child page opens only after the original addressed inspect confirms the exact parent-child lineage; stale connections and mismatched catalog rows cannot navigate. Parent chat route and draft remain in place. The Web docked sidebar tab, at-reference source and full original observations remain incomplete; device behavior is unverified.

Native @ discovery calls the original fileReferences and sessionReferenceResolver services, retains exact path/canonical Session mentions, and separates folder selection from descent. Owner-bound cancellation and query/connection invalidation reject late results. Sent references follow original UTF-16 and recorded-label rules; file chips open the source Session reader, while folder/Session chips remain labels. Real Android-profile host discovery and focused widgets pass; phone acceptance is unverified.

The App stages the original pure matcher and applies its UTF-16 ranges before other references in sent user text. Host matcher and Flutter rendering tests pass; Android device display and every original formatter combination remain unverified.

Shared job record streaming and stop requests exist. An Android-private type/time receipt makes a lost runtime visible on the task page after restart without claiming a task result or replaying work. Unplanned Service destruction after Node admission synchronously records the interruption and ends the dedicated process, rather than leaving an ownerless Node behind. Planned Service replacement now rechecks the original Agent, inbox, job and plugin-operation registries at reservation and commit, refusing active or unknown work while accepting safely settled work; host tests cover an Agent/job starting between the checks. Abrupt OS process death cannot run the Service callback, and a new task starting after the final Node acknowledgment remains a shutdown race requiring device acceptance. Task history still needs the original cold Session recovery read. Complete original output/terminal behavior, detached child supervision and device notification delivery remain unverified.
Shared schedule listing/edit/delete and delivery records exist; complete original lifecycle/device acceptance remains open.

Native goal creation with an optional round cap, current-goal presentation, edit, pause, resume and clear use the original goal service and sequenced Session projection. Host lifecycle, stale-revision and process-local activation transitions have focused Flutter tests. Complete original behavior and device interaction remain unverified.

Bare /feedback opens a category-and-remark form that records through the original sessionFeedback service without starting a model turn; typed /feedback <text> remains the original command. Both forms share one taxonomy/editor. Unknown transport outcomes preserve the draft and block automatic duplicate submission. Host projection, route, command, and failure tests pass; device behavior and complete original feedback semantics remain unverified.

Original host workflow plugins remain disabled and are omitted from the Android preset. A distinct native V8 workflow entry reuses the original workflow tool definition, single-use admission, live parent ToolRuntime identity and original jobs registry behind MODEL_WORKFLOW_DEVICE_ACCEPTED=false. Newly activated children inherit only the live parent's reviewed first-party read/glob/grep/write/edit/web_search/web_fetch/linux_exec/linux_import/linux_export/linux_inspect registrations. App files stay inside activation-pinned scope and current parent/child permission roots; original observation and web-provider checks remain. Linux requires existing parent registration and remains absent under the closed production Linux gate. Its disk belongs to the child Session, with no guest network or App-UID Shell; persistence intersects activation permission and current parent/child policies, while transfers require all three to permit writing. One App-wide Linux execution slot requires serial Linux steps; busy means no native dispatch, not automatic replay. Limits remain 8 total and 2 concurrent children over 120 seconds with the parent model route. No PTC, recursive delegation or cross-Session SAF/attachment grants are delegated; cold resume alone restores no file/web/Linux grants. Host child, ToolRuntime, receipt and durable Session tests do not establish production availability or device lifecycle acceptance.

Original host workflow plugins remain disabled and are omitted from the Android preset. A distinct native V8 workflow entry reuses the original workflow tool definition, single-use admission, live parent ToolRuntime identity and original jobs registry behind MODEL_WORKFLOW_DEVICE_ACCEPTED=false. Newly activated children inherit only the live parent's reviewed first-party read/glob/grep/write/edit/web_search/web_fetch/linux_exec/linux_import/linux_export/linux_inspect registrations. App files stay inside activation-pinned scope and current parent/child permission roots; original observation and web-provider checks remain. Linux requires existing parent registration and remains absent under the closed production Linux gate. Its disk belongs to the child Session, with no guest network or App-UID Shell; persistence intersects activation permission and current parent/child policies, while transfers require all three to permit writing. Limits remain 8 total and 2 concurrent children over 120 seconds with the parent model route. No PTC, recursive delegation or cross-Session SAF/attachment grants are delegated; cold resume alone restores no file/web/Linux grants. Host child, ToolRuntime, receipt and durable Session tests do not establish production availability or device lifecycle acceptance.

sourceDigestPolicy: SHA256 of the corresponding inert YAML row encoded as sorted object keys, preserved array order and typed scalar values. Comments and YAML key order do not affect the digest; config, disabled expressions and nested declarations do.

capabilities.title: Conversation and Agent loop
capabilities.remaining: Confirm streamed replies, cancellation, retry, and stable reading position in the installed App; carrier wiring does not prove all upstream Agent semantics.

capabilities.title: Models, credentials and account
capabilities.remaining: Confirm real sign-in return, avatar refresh, provider switching, persisted default reasoning selection and requests after upgrade.

capabilities.title: Authorized files, images and search
capabilities.remaining: Verify original tools and android_files through real model calls, granted and revoked SAF providers, large-file cancellation and workspace isolation. Directory editor view and binary document ingestion are not equivalent to desktop file access.

capabilities.title: Workspaces and file changes
capabilities.remaining: Confirm per-session working directories, changes and restoration after process death without changing other sessions.

capabilities.title: Durable sessions, search and export
capabilities.remaining: Complete ordinary APK upgrade and interrupted-write recovery with saved sessions, settings, credentials and attachments; exercise content search and export on retained data.

capabilities.title: Goals, plans and context compaction
capabilities.remaining: Verify plan approval, goal continuation, compaction and their persisted state through native controls and real requests.

capabilities.title: Subagents and follow-up
capabilities.remaining: Verify spawn, fork, follow-up, cancellation and parent/child ownership on device, including process retirement.

capabilities.title: Background jobs and schedules
capabilities.remaining: Complete lock-screen, network-loss recovery, cancellation, process death and scheduled-task acceptance with bounded live work and accurate completion state.

capabilities.title: Shell and terminal execution
capabilities.remaining: General App-UID shell is unavailable by default. Isolated linux_exec is wired behind a closed device gate and can satisfy bounded guest shell operations after image and production-device acceptance. Interactive terminal sessions, guest-to-App output files and original desktop Bash process semantics are separate limits. Windows PowerShell is not an Android requirement.

capabilities.title: Programmatic tools and workflows
capabilities.remaining: Reviewed android_ptc and workflows with reviewed child file/web/Linux tools are implemented behind closed source gates. Workflow children receive only current parent first-party read/glob/grep/write/edit/web_search/web_fetch/linux_exec/linux_import/linux_export/linux_inspect registrations, with live identity, parent/child policy and activation-workspace checks. Linux tools require existing parent registration and use a child-Session-private offline disk; persistence intersects activation and current policies, transfers require writable activation and current parent/child permissions, and one App-wide slot requires serial Linux steps. Cold resume restores no grant. Accept the production Node-to-native ToolRuntime path, bounded results, real file/web/Linux callbacks, cancellation and retirement, background child ownership and cold/process-death recovery before opening them. General Node APIs, PTC images, child App-UID Shell/recursive delegation and arbitrary child tool definitions remain outside the reviewed subset; do not describe it as full upstream PTC parity. Reviewed PTC can call the parent's original four Linux tools with live policy and durable receipts; the actual device import/execute/export chain remains unaccepted.

capabilities.title: Lightweight Linux guest
capabilities.remaining: TinyEMU isolated-UID Linux execution and authorized 64 MiB workspace import/export are implemented behind LINUX_VM_DEVICE_ACCEPTED=false. ToolRuntime resolves live session policy: read-only execution discards disk changes and file transfer requires write permission. A workflow child may inherit the original Linux tools only from live parent registrations; its disk remains private to its Session, permissions intersect the activation grant and current parent/child policies, and cold resume restores no grant. The App has one Linux execution slot, so workflow Linux steps must be serialized. An offline Alpine candidate with Python, Git and curl has host execution and filesystem checks, exact image/build evidence and a verified corresponding-source archive. Explicit Alpine release candidate packaging verifies exact assets, native provider and corresponding sources; switching back to the ordinary build is checked for residual guest assets. Production enablement and device acceptance remain: verify model calls, file-transfer hashes/readback and no-overwrite publication, writable persistence, read-only discard, cancellation and upgrade recovery on the installed APK. Read-only linux_inspect and first-execution recovery checks report durable publication facts and block unresolved or review-required Sessions without replay. There is no acknowledgement/unlock API, and retirement after owner-process death remains unverified. Python standard-library analysis is covered by a device fixture but is not yet device-certified. Bounded guest HTTPS GET uses dsh-fetch with exact-host and native one-time approval; its production approval, cancellation and real device network path remain unaccepted. General guest networking is absent; installed curl and Git do not receive raw network access. Host checks do not discharge these device and image-delivery requirements.

capabilities.title: Web retrieval and remote access
capabilities.remaining: Verify configured search/fetch providers, local phone proxy, network-loss recovery and browser authority; inherited MCP resource support still needs a native invocation and permissions audit.

capabilities.title: Plugins and settings
capabilities.remaining: Verify install/update/rollback, protected host configuration, unsupported package handling and settings persistence in the installed runtime.

capabilities.title: Native presentation and localization
capabilities.remaining: Native Flutter replaces browser component execution. Confirm compact reasoning display, blur transitions and unchanged reply position; a full multilingual native localization contract remains absent.

capabilities.title: Feedback and telemetry consent
capabilities.remaining: Verify consent, selected-prefix export, cancellation and offline failure without treating configured exporters as successful uploads.

capabilities.title: Document preview and office authoring
capabilities.remaining: Preview exists with bounds. SDK office authoring skills and workspace dependency runtime are not composed into Android; file conversion and complete editing workflows need separate delivery and device evidence.

capabilities.title: Alternative CLI and SDK entrypoints
capabilities.remaining: Headless command-line, stdio SDK and ACP launch modes are not Android native entrypoints. Their shared user capabilities remain assigned to the corresponding groups.
